title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's go-to-market messaging and sales assets for engineers, solutions architects, and field sellers. It includes: positioning and core messaging, competitive brief summaries, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance and examples, representative case studies, and a curated Security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use this as the single-source-of-truth for customer-facing positioning and to prepare deal-specific materials.

Audience

- Field sales (AE/SE)
- Solutions architects and pre-sales engineers
- Customer Success and post-sales onboarding
- Marketing and product marketing for collateral alignment

Key Objectives

1. Provide consistent, production-focused positioning that differentiates Redwood on latency, economics, and operational controls.
2. Give sellers concrete competitive talking points and rebuttals tied to measurable outcomes (latency, cost per token, SLOs).
3. Offer repeatable pitch deck structure and pricing examples for common deal shapes (self-serve, dedicated, private).
4. Surface customer success stories and measurable impact metrics for reference in discovery and demos.
5. Equip sellers with a security FAQ and references to ease procurement and legal evaluation.

Core Positioning and One-Liners

- Developer-first inference platform focused on production economics: predictable latency, cost controls, and flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
- For engineering teams that need reliable LLM serving at scale, Redwood replaces fragile DIY stacks with a unified runtime, rollout controls, and observability tailored to LLM workloads.

Elevator Pitches (30s / 1 min)

- 30s: "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first inference runtime and control plane so engineering teams can ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 1m: "We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing, and workload-aware caching to deliver consistent per-request latency and lower per-token cost. Customers move from ad-hoc infra to an opinionated, observable platform with built-in rollout controls, quantization guidance, and enterprise-ready security for regulated workflows."

Value Propositions by Persona

- Product/Engineering: Reduce time-to-production, avoid building model serving internals, predictable latency and per-token cost, integrated model versioning and rollouts.
- Platform/Infra: Standardized runtime across teams, capacity isolation (Dedicated), private control plane options, autoscaling and SLA-backed throughput.
- Security/Compliance: Audit logging, KMS/HSM integrations, VPC/on-prem options and evidence for common compliance frameworks.
- Finance/Procurement: Usage-based pricing for hosted, reserved contracts for dedicated capacity, clear unit economics and cost-avoidance via caching and batching.

Competitive Briefs (high-level summaries + talking points)

1) Major cloud AI providers (managed endpoints)
- Short: Offer broad model access and infra, but often lack inference-optimized runtimes, deep LLM-specific observability, and flexible private deployment bundles.
- Differentiators: Redwood emphasizes runtime optimizations (kernel selection, continuous batching), developer-first SDKs, and private deployment parity.
- Rebuttal: "If you need predictable latency at scale and private deployment parity, Redwood ships the runtime and controls teams need today without building internal infra."

2) LLM API-focused vendors (simplicity-first providers)
- Short: Great for quick proofs-of-concept; may not scale cost-effectively for high-throughput production.
- Differentiators: Redwood provides cost controls (batching, quantization profiles), routing policies, and dedicated capacity for predictable economics.
- Rebuttal: "For high-volume production usage, the cost delta and lack of rollout controls on lightweight APIs lead to operational risk and unpredictable bills."

3) Self-hosted inference vendors / on-prem runtimes
- Short: Customers building their own stack get control but face long payoff times and operational risk.
- Differentiators: Redwood offers both private/on-prem and managed options with engineering support, audit logs, and simpler model lifecycle management.
- Rebuttal: "Redwood reduces time-to-value with a combined offering: deploy privately when required and leverage our operational experience and SLAs."

Competitive Metrics to Reference (internal benchmarking)

- Median 99th-percentile token latency (short prompt): 50-80ms on verified configurations (varies by model family and GPU class). Use internal perf briefs for exact numbers per model/hardware.
- Typical per-token cost reduction vs unoptimized single-request serving: 20-60% via batching and caching.
- Dedicated capacity SLA: 99.9% uptime for production-tier pools (example contract language available in the contract templates).

Pitch Deck Guidance (structure + slide checklist)

Use the canonical pitch deck template (link in related assets). Recommended slide order:
1. Title & 1-line value prop
2. Customer pain + market context (latency, cost, ops pain)
3. Redwood solution overview (runtime + control plane + deployment choices)
4. Key differentiators (runtime optimizations, unified interface, cost controls)
5. Demo / architecture diagram (show routing, KV cache, autoscaling)
6. Performance & economics (benchmarks, typical cost savings, latency SLOs)
7. Security & compliance (audit logs, VPC, KMS integrations)
8. Pricing & proposed deal structure (example numbers; see Pricing Guidance)
9. Case study / customer outcomes
10. Next steps / pilot proposal / success criteria

Slide tips:
- Keep technical diagrams at the level of a solutions architect: show components and flows, not internal code.
- Use per-route dashboards screenshots from Redwood Console for production credibility.
- Tailor pricing examples to the prospect's expected throughput (tokens/month) and deployment mode.

Pricing Guidance (example deal shapes and guardrails)

Pricing Overview (product tiers)
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based pricing with per-token generation and embedding rates, tiered discounts at volume thresholds.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commits, overage rules, and burst options.
- Private: platform license + optional managed services / implementation fees; negotiable for enterprise deals.

Sample pricing examples (illustrative only)
- Mid-market SaaS pilot (hosted): 100M gen tokens/mo -> list price estimate: $X per 1M tokens with 10% volume discount (replace X with current published rates; consult pricing spreadsheet).
- Dedicated pilot: 1 reserved GPU pool (e.g., 8xA100-equivalent) for predictable throughput; monthly commit pricing with 12-month term.
- Enterprise private deployment: platform license + implementation (one-time) + 24/7 support addon.

Pricing guardrails for sellers
- Always consult pricing_ops@redwood.com for >$250k ARR deals and any private deployment negotiations.
- Do not promise custom SLAs or pricing outside published contract templates without legal and finance approval.
- Use the pricing spreadsheet and ROI calculator (linked in assets) to produce customer-specific estimates.

Case Studies (recommended structure for inclusion)

Each case study should include: customer background, problem statement, technical solution (architecture and deployment mode), measurable outcomes (latency, cost, feature velocity), timeline, and references/contacts.

Example summary (anonymized for GTM use)
- Customer: High-growth conversational AI SaaS
- Challenge: Unpredictable latency and 3-4x cost variability from ad-hoc model serving; delayed feature launches due to infra work.
- Solution: Moved to Redwood Dedicated, used autoscaling and KV prefix caching, pinned model versions and canary rollouts.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in per-token cost (estimated), 3x improvement in 99th-pct latency, two-week reduction in feature rollout time.

Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for common questions)

Q: Where does customer data live and how is it protected?
A: Data residency options include region selection for hosted deployments, VPC/private deployments for network isolation, and on-prem installs when required. All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption is supported via provider-managed keys, and KMS/HSM integrations are available for enterprise customers.

Q: Can I use my own KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores where required.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs include request metadata, model version, route, and operator actions. Logs can be exported to S3, SIEMs, or a customer-managed logging endpoint depending on the deployment type.

Q: How do you handle PII and redaction?
A: Redwood provides configurable request/response masking and support for ingestion-time redaction patterns. We also document recommended prompt engineering patterns to minimize sensitive data exposure.

Q: Do you sign standard infosec contracts (DPA, SOC2, ISO) and can you provide evidence?
A: Yes. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report, standard DPA template, and can provide ISO-related evidence for enterprise engagements. See security-and-compliance evidence pages for details.

Q: How are model updates and rollouts controlled to avoid regressions?
A: Redwood provides version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback policies. Quality monitoring can be tied to prompt sets and regression alerts to prevent silent quality drops.

Sales Enablement Playbook: How to use this doc

1. Prep: Review the Pitch Deck Guidance and Pricing Guidance before calls.
2. Discovery: Use the Value Propositions by Persona to map to stakeholder priorities.
3. Demo: Show Console per-route dashboards and architecture diagram.
4. Follow-up: Include a case study tailored to the prospect and attach the security FAQ.
5. Handoff: For closed deals requiring Dedicated or Private, engage customer_success and eng-private-deployments for onboarding and runbook transfer.
